notes: Masses and shares are from Steelcase's 2023 EPD for the Leap task chair/stool (product codes beginning 462 for the Americas, plus APAC codes). The typical configuration is a stool with a steel base, the lowest-impact chair has a plastic base and the highest-impact APAC configuration an aluminium base, so check the base before using the figures.

gaps: The EPD models a stool (product 46267179, steel base) as typical, a chair with a plastic base (46216179) as lowest impact, and an APAC configuration (codes beginning LEAP-, aluminium base, headrest, lumbar support) as highest impact; the last is not one of the 462 codes.

The EPD does not use the name V2. A dealer sheet and a parts seller use "Leap V2", and no page read links the EPD's 462 product codes to that name, so the model is named as the EPD names it (the record id still ends in v2).

Weight conflict, not reconciled: the dealer sheet gives the Leap V2 as 46.7 lb with 400 lb capacity; the EPD composition totals are 24.760 kg, 27.231 kg and 32.786 kg, all above 46.7 lb when converted (24.760 kg is about 54.6 lb). Each is kept as its source states it.

Gas cylinder left out: the only source is a VXB listing for an aftermarket replacement cylinder for post-2009 Leap V2 chairs (5 in stroke, 'Class 4' in the seller's wording). It is not an OEM source and not tied to the EPD codes; the EPD says only height-adjustable seat.
The EPD names polyurethane but not whether it is seat foam, so the foam_rubber claim gives the material only.
Caster size, stem and count, and any tilt spring, are not given; the EPD says only hard casters.
method: NSF EPD 10812, Steelcase Leap (Americas and APAC), issued 17 February 2023, read with research tool pdf: p.2 coverage, p.3 scope and SKUs, p.5 typical configuration composition, p.7 lowest-impact composition, p.9 highest-impact composition.
POI Store seating comparison sheet (dealer PDF), read with research tool pdf: Leap V2 column, 400 lb capacity and 46.7 lb weight; used only for the weight conflict above.
VXB replacement gas lift cylinder listing (WebFetch): seller's wording on stroke, class and fit; used only for the gas cylinder gap above.
The researcher reported steelcase.com pages as HTTP 403 and Crandall Office pages as rate-limited; they were not re-opened.

comps.spec: Base differs by EPD configuration: steel base on the typical stool (steel is 20.978 kg, 64.00% of its composition), plastic base on the lowest-impact chair, aluminium base on the highest-impact APAC configuration
Hard casters in the typical stool, the lowest-impact chair and the highest-impact configuration
Polyurethane (PU): 1.789 kg (5.50%) of the typical stool's composition and 1.789 kg (7.20%) of the lowest-impact chair's; the typical stool has an upholstered seat and back
Upholstered seat and back in the typical stool and in the highest-impact configuration
Nylon (PA6 and PA66): 4.100 kg (12.51%) of the typical stool and 5.050 kg (20.40%) of the lowest-impact chair
Polypropylene (PP): 3.068 kg (9.40%) of the typical stool and 2.811 kg (11.40%) of the lowest-impact chair
